summary: The nonfatal threshold is valid Stata and behaves as documented, but it removes the guarantee that the target-only and all-record linkage runs differ solely through model-name targeting. Before interpreting that comparison, classify the 436 discrepancies by target status and either eliminate consequential differences or quantify their effect on links.

findings.title: Permitted fallback discrepancies can make the linkage runs differ for reasons other than target-only substitution
findings.what_the_code_does: The code counts discrepancies with `name_true_cleaned_exists==0 & !(f_name==f_ans & l_name==l_ans)` but now exits only when ``nbad' > 0.001*`nchk'`. Thus the documented 436 discrepancies are allowed. For a discrepant non-target record, lines 111-114 put `_ans_cleaned` names into the target-only input, while the all-record baseline retains the differing `_true_cleaned` fallback, even though neither difference represents use of a model name.
findings.why_it_matters: If any of the 436 records are non-targets, the intended comparison is not an exact target-only versus all-record model-name counterfactual. Different fallback cleaning can alter those records' links and, through uniqueness or candidate competition, potentially other links. The affected result may be negligible, but the current global 0.1% tolerance does not establish that.
findings.how_to_check: Before replacement, run `count if name_true_cleaned_exists==0 & !(f_name==f_ans & l_name==l_ans) & !tgt` and tabulate the discrepancies by `tgt`. After producing both link files, merge them by census ID and count changed link assignments involving these IDs or their competing candidates.
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile the two fallback-cleaning paths or require zero discrepancies specifically among non-target records. If proceeding temporarily, report the consequential non-target count and show that excluding those records and affected candidate sets does not change the comparison.

verified_clean.item: The target-only substitution itself remains correctly conditioned on non-target status.
verified_clean.evidence: Only records satisfying `!tgt` receive `_ans_cleaned` first name, last name, middle initial, and model-existence status at MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:111-114.

verified_clean.item: The discrepancy denominator and numerator are accumulated across every birthplace file rather than only the final iteration.
verified_clean.evidence: `nchk` and `nbad` are initialized before the loop and incremented from `r(N)` inside it at MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:85-109.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so paper claims could not be checked against the code; claims-vs-code review was limited to statements in code comments and the supplied review brief.
The external census and divided-file datasets were unavailable, so the documented 436 discrepancies could not be independently reproduced or classified by target status.
The Stata pipeline could not be executed; runtime conclusions are based on source semantics and counts documented in review/briefs/2026-11-17-tgt-check-nonfatal.md.
This was a diff-scoped review of the uncommitted working tree, including every untracked file reported by `git status --short`, not a full-repository audit.
